cues.en: Why should an obvious innuendo still feel more comfortable than a direct overture that is in some sense on the record?
cues.zh: 为什么一个明显的暗示，仍然比一个某种意义上已经摆在台面上的直接示好，让人感觉更自在？

cues.en: To illustrate the problem with a a scene from the romantic comedy When Harry Met Sally,
cues.zh: 用浪漫喜剧《当哈利遇到莎莉》中的一个场景来说明这个问题，

cues.en: where in an early scene of the movie,

cues.en: Harry makes a remark that Sally interprets as sexual, and she accuses him of, you're coming on to me. So he says, well, what do you want me to do about it? I take it back. Okay? I take it back. She says, you can't take it back.
cues.zh: 哈利说了一句话，莎莉把它理解为性暗示，于是指责他说，你在勾引我。他就说，那你想让我怎么办？我收回。行了吧？我收回。她说，你收不回去。

cues.en: Why not? Because it's already out there. He says, oh, jeez. What are we supposed to do? Call the cops? It's already out there.

cues.en: Well, what is the psychological
cues.zh: 那么，一个我们觉得已经说出去、已经摆在台面上的示好，

cues.en: status of an overture that we feel to be out there or on the record that makes it feel so much more awkward than a veiled overture that's conveyed indirectly?
cues.zh: 它的心理状态到底是什么，为什么它比一个间接传达的含蓄示好让人尴尬得多？

cues.en: And I think a key to this paradox
cues.zh: 我认为解开这个悖论的关键，

cues.en: is a concept that economists
cues.zh: 在于一个经济学家

cues.en: and logicians call mutual knowledge,
cues.zh: 和逻辑学家称为“共同知识”的概念，

cues.en: which they distinguish from individual knowledge.
cues.zh: 他们把它与个体知识区分开来。

cues.en: In individual knowledge, A knows X and B knows X.
cues.zh: 在个体知识中，A知道X，B也知道X。

cues.en: In mutual knowledge, A knows x, B knows x, A knows that B knows x, B knows that A knows x,
cues.zh: 在共同知识中，A知道X，B知道X，A知道B知道X，B知道A知道X，

cues.en: A knows that B knows that A knows x,

cues.en: And this is a difference that has profound consequences.
cues.zh: 而这个差别有着深远的后果。
